Areas I commonly work with

I tend to work with adults experiencing anxiety, life transitions, relationship conflict, and the impacts of chronic stress. My approach centers safety, practical skills, and collaborative goals.

Request a consultation
Anxiety & Worry

I help people build sustainable ways to reduce rumination, manage panic moments, and regain confidence in daily functioning using behavioral tools and pacing.

Trauma-Informed Support

Trauma can show up as hypervigilance, avoidance, or numbness. I offer grounding, stabilization, and paced processing while prioritizing safety and consent.

Relationship Work

Whether it’s communication patterns, boundary-setting, or separation, I work with individuals and couples to clarify needs and practices that shift interactions toward safety.

Burnout & Work Stress

When work overwhelms, we explore systems-level thinking, rest strategies, and values-aligned changes to reduce exhaustion without shame.

Transitions & Life Shifts

Big life changes—relocation, parenting, job shifts—bring grief and growth. Therapy can be a navigational practice during these times.

Self-Compassion & Identity

Work that centers how you treat yourself and how you relate to identity-related stressors, including shame, cultural experiences, and belonging.

Which path fits you?

I offer a few ways to work together depending on goals:

  • Short-term Focus — 6–12 sessions to learn tools and tackle a specific problem.
  • Supportive Ongoing Therapy — weekly or biweekly sessions for deeper, steady work.
  • The Resilience Intensive — a single extended session for targeted work and planning. (Ask about availability.)
Pricing and sliding-scale options are discussed at intake; I provide superbills for insurance reimbursement.

Try a short checklist

Download a 3-minute symptom checklist to help decide which area feels most urgent. Enter your email and it will be sent to you.

Questions specific to specialties

How do you handle cultural differences?
I work collaboratively to understand your background and preferences. I adapt interventions to be culturally attuned and respectful.
Will you diagnose me?
When helpful, I discuss diagnostic impressions to guide care, but the focus will be on practical steps and your priorities rather than labels alone.
{{BUSINESS_NAME}} • Confidentiality considered and upheld; limits include risk of harm to self/others, subpoenas, and mandated reporting. Not an emergency service. If you are in crisis, call emergency services or a crisis line in your area.

Care that is pragmatic and warm
Home Paths Meet Book
Therapeutic stance

Collaborative, paced, and rooted in safety

I work to create a predictable, compassionate space. We build direction together: stabilization and skills first, deeper processing as you feel ready. The process prioritizes consent and client control.

I do not provide crisis services. If you are in immediate danger, contact local emergency services. Confidentiality is honored except where safety requires disclosure by law.
{{THERAPIST_NAME}}, {{LICENSE}}
{{MODALITIES}}
{{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}}

Programs & offerings

The Focused Series

A 6-8 session structured plan for a specific goal (e.g., reduce panic attacks, manage work stress). Homework and skill coaching included.

Format: Weekly 50-min sessions
Renewal Intensive

A single extended session (120–180 minutes) to jump-start a plan, stabilize symptoms, or map out concrete next steps. Best for people who need focused momentum.

Format: One extended appointment
Open Support

Ongoing weekly or biweekly therapy for deeper work on patterns, relationships, or identity development. Emphasis on long-term coping and meaning-making.

Consultation & Coaching

Short blocks for practical skill-building around sleep, boundaries, or workplace communication. Not a replacement for specialty treatment.

A pragmatic weekly rhythm

  1. Intake: We explore goals, history, safety, and scheduling preferences.
  2. Plan: We co-create a short plan with markers for progress and check-ins.
  3. Practice: Sessions include skill teaching, reflection, and real-world practice tasks.
  4. Review: Every 6–8 sessions we review progress and adjust the plan.

Investment & scheduling

I aim to be transparent: I discuss current rates during the intake conversation and offer limited sliding-scale availability. Many clients use packages (e.g., 6-session block) for continuity; superbills are available for insurance reimbursement.

Specific costs are given in a private conversation and depend on session length and format. This site does not replace personalized assessment.

Common process questions

How quickly will I feel better?
Progress varies. Some notice relief in a few sessions with focused tools; deeper shifts often take months. We set short-term goals to measure change together.
Can I switch between in-person and telehealth?
Yes—where licensure allows, we will discuss logistics and preferences so care remains consistent.

Ready to begin?

Schedule an intake
By contacting me you consent to an initial scheduling conversation; therapy is voluntary. For emergencies, call your local crisis resources.
